title: Daimon eval bundle, format 1.0
description: Every JSON document in a Daimon eval bundle. Each document names its type in `schema`. Validate a file against the whole schema, or one type with #/$defs/<Type>.

Ext.description: Free-form extension data. Keys are namespaced (`vendor.key`). Readers ignore what they do not know.

Glob.description: `*` matches any run of characters except `.` and `/`; `**` matches anything.

BlobRef.description: A file in blobs/sha256/<sha256>. Content-addressed; the same bytes are stored once.

Body.description: A payload: inline text, inline JSON, or a blob. Exactly one.

PrincipalRef.description: Who: a person, group or agent of the deployment, or an opaque label in exported data.

label.description: Human label, e.g. staging. Never a hostname or tenant id.

instance.description: Opaque stable hash of the exporting deployment.

files.description: Every non-blob file in the bundle except bundle.json, with its hash.

policy.description: Scrub policy name and version, e.g. default/1.

unchecked_blobs.description: Blobs still flagged for a human check.

includes_identities.description: True only when reviewer and owner identities were kept instead of labels.

value.description: Base64 signature over the RFC 8785 canonical form of this manifest without `signature`.

scrub.description: rebuilt: text file rewritten with fakes; redacted: image or binary with regions masked; clean: checked, nothing to scrub; generated: produced in an enclosed run from fake data; unscrubbed: raw.

ToolAlias.description: Maps a tool name seen in recorded data to the name or effect used when matching. Lets baselines and live agents with different tool names share expectations.

args_map.description: Target arg pointer -> source arg pointer.

Case.description: One line of suites/<id>/cases.jsonl. A fixed conversation history plus the next turn, the recorded world it runs in, scripted actions and expectations.

hash.description: sha256 of the RFC 8785 canonical form of this case without `hash`.

source_thread.description: Opaque key of the source conversation. Cases from one thread share it; stats cluster on it.

source_turn.description: Index of the tested turn within the source thread.

dedupe_group.description: Cases judged near-duplicates share a group; thinning keeps a few per group.

history.description: Messages before the tested turn, oldest first, as the platform would show them.

level.description: full: messages, tool calls and results; tools: calls without some results; text: messages only; authored: written, not recorded.

source_system.description: Generic label of the system the case came from, e.g. baseline-a.

source_ref.description: Opaque, non-reversible reference (keyed hash) to the source record.

entities.description: Count of distinct real entities replaced. The mapping itself is never in a bundle.

now.description: Time the tested turn was sent. The agent's clock starts here in case-clock mode.

timezone.description: IANA name for the requester, e.g. Europe/Berlin.

Surface.description: Where the conversation happens and who is in it. All names are fakes after scrubbing.

id.description: Platform-shaped fake id, stable across the suite for the same real person.

author.description: Participant id, or the bot's id.

state.description: missing: no bytes kept; the agent sees an unavailable file.

description.description: What the file showed, for judges and the simulator when bytes are missing or redacted.

Turn.description: The tested turn: one or more requester messages sent together (debounced DMs send several).

Script.description: What the simulated people do while the agent works.

question.description: When the agent asks the requester something no step answers: end the item, or let the simulator reply as the requester.

max_follow_ups.description: Extra requester turns (reply steps or simulated answers) allowed in one item.

target.description: `matched` (the trigger's message or card, default), `last_bot_message`, or a message id.

fields.description: Form field id -> value. Fake values only.

World.description: Everything outside the agent that the run may touch, as recorded or authored. The fake world answers from this, then from the per-item overlay, then from the simulator.

vars.description: Non-secret variables set in the sandbox. Secrets come from identities.

instructions.description: Facts the simulator must hold to, beyond the recorded data.

Exchange.description: One recorded or derived request and its answer.

surface.description: mcp: an MCP tool call; http: one HTTP request; cli: a command line and its output (evidence; compiled to http before runs); provider_tool: a provider-side tool such as web search.

service.description: Canonical service, e.g. github, git, google.drive, web, daimon.

server.description: MCP server name for mcp exchanges.

tool.description: Tool name for mcp and provider_tool exchanges.

verified.description: Derived exchanges: true when replaying the recorded command reproduced the recorded output.

derived_from.description: The cli exchange this http exchange was compiled from.

repeatable.description: False: answers once; a second identical call falls through to the overlay or simulator.

args.description: mcp and provider_tool: the call's arguments.

shell.description: The full shell line when argv was split from it.

Match.description: How a live request is matched to this exchange.

mode.description: normalized: canonical JSON, query order, whitespace and default args ignored; keys: only `keys` compared; semantic: the simulator model decides equivalence.

Resource.description: Seed state of one service object (issue, doc, sheet, calendar event, page). Writes in a run change a per-item copy.

blob.description: File content for documents, decks and sheets.

path.description: Absolute path in the sandbox at the start of the turn.

url.description: Clone URL as the agent uses it (fake owner and name).

bundle.description: A git bundle with the refs below. Pushes land in a per-item copy.

cloned_at.description: Sandbox path where the repo is already checked out, if it was at turn start.

McpServer.description: An MCP server the agent had. Daimon's own tools come from the deployment; third-party and relayed servers need their recorded catalogue here.

Identity.description: An account the agent acts as. Runs mint fresh fake tokens of the right shape; none are stored.

token_env.description: Sandbox variable that carries the fake token, e.g. GH_TOKEN.

token_shape.description: Token format to mint, e.g. github_pat, google_oauth.

passthrough.description: Extra exact hosts reached for real, read-only. Needs an admin-allowed list.

deny.description: Hosts refused outright instead of simulated.

SimEntry.description: A simulator answer kept so every arm and repeat gets the same one.

key.description: sha256 of the normalized request plus the overlay state it saw.

AgentContext.description: What the deployment knew about the conversation at turn time, outside the chat history.

context.description: Context-provider output injected at turn start.

previous_session.description: Hand-off summary from an earlier session, when the platform carried one over.

mode.description: strict: same calls, same order; unordered: same calls, any order; subset: these calls appear, others allowed; superset: no calls beyond these.

note.description: What a good answer must contain, when no single reference fits.

criterion.description: op llm: what a judge model checks, answered yes, no or unknown.

WorldCheck.description: A check on the per-item world state after the run.

criterion.description: One yes/no question, or a scale with anchors.

hard.description: A failed hard item fails the case whatever the score.

Arm.description: One side of a comparison: a live Daimon agent configuration or a recorded baseline.

agent.description: Agent name on the deployment that ran it.

agent_snapshot.description: Exported agent definition (no credentials) for reproduction elsewhere.

overrides.description: Settings changed for this arm only.

case_ids.description: Subset run; absent means every case of the suite version.

blind_labels.description: Arm id -> neutral label shown in blind review.

RunItem.description: One line of runs/<id>/items.jsonl: one case, one arm, one repeat.

EventStream.description: Transcript events inline, or a blob of NDJSON TranscriptEvent lines when large.

turn.description: 0 for the tested turn; 1+ for scripted follow-ups.

redacted.description: True for thinking or text the provider withheld.

Origin.description: Where an answer came from. sandbox: computed inside the sandbox; live: a recorded baseline's real answer.

WorldCall.description: A request that reached the fake world in a run, with the answer given.

reason.description: Why it was denied or simulated.

ChatEvent.description: What the simulated chat surface showed, in platform-neutral form.

scripted.description: Script step id when a simulated person did this.

platform_payloads.description: The native payload each platform would have received, for previews.

Output.description: A file the agent produced or delivered.

source.description: chat_upload: sent into the chat; sandbox: left in the output folder; artifact: published link; world: written to a fake service such as a doc or deck.

renders.description: Page or slide images (PNG), in order.

text.description: Extracted text for search, diff and judges.

Enclosure.description: How enclosed one item was, so results from different setups are not compared blindly.

mode.description: recorded: a baseline item that ran against the real world.

real_time_binaries.description: Probed binaries that ignore the case clock.

substitutions.description: Provider tools swapped for enclosed ones, e.g. web_search -> eval web search.

Score.description: One line of runs/<id>/scores.jsonl. Every grader (code, model, person, agent) writes this shape.

pair.description: Pairwise scores name two items instead of one.

criterion.description: Check path (e.g. tool_calls/0) or rubric item id, or `overall`.

Anchor.description: Points at a part of an item: a message, tool call, file page, image region, table range, text span or card element.

ref.description: Message id, call_id, world call seq or output id.

quote.description: The anchored text, so the anchor survives small re-renders.

ReviewRecord.description: One line of runs/<id>/reviews.jsonl: a review queue or a comment. Verdicts are Scores.
